option_mapping.Meryl Streep: Considered before casting; not in the final film

sources.title: AFI Catalog: Thelma & Louise (1991)
supports: Susan Sarandon is credited as Louise Elizabeth Sawyer; Davis is Thelma Dickinson and Keitel is Hal Slocumbe.
Khouri wrote the film; Scott directed; Biddle photographed it; Noble edited; Zimmer composed the music.
AFI records Davis and Sarandon’s 1990 casting and says Streep and Goldie Hawn had earlier been contenders.
sources.limits: Louise and the plot are fictional. Streep’s earlier consideration is not a final-film credit.

sources.organization: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: The 64th Academy Awards (1992)
supports: The Academy film-summary header reports five grouped nomination categories and one win, while the category roster contains six individual nomination entries because Davis and Sarandon are separately listed in Actress in a Leading Role.
Biddle, Scott, and Noble received the other individual nominations.
sources.limits: The 1992 ceremony follows the 1991 release and supports only its listed award outcomes.

question_sources.film: One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest

sources.title: AFI Catalog: One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest (1975)
supports: Jack Nicholson is credited as Randle Patrick McMurphy; the listed distractors play Nurse Ratched, Martini, and Chief Bromden.
The film adapts Wasserman’s play, itself based on Kesey’s 1962 novel.
AFI records the Oregon State Hospital shoot and credits Jack Nitzsche for original music.
sources.limits: The hospital and its patients are fictional dramatic material; they do not establish medical or psychiatric facts about real care or diagnoses.

sources.organization: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: The 48th Academy Awards (1976)
supports: One Flew over the Cuckoo’s Nest received nine nominations and five wins.
Nicholson won Actor, Fletcher won Actress, Forman won Directing, and the film won Best Picture and Adapted Screenplay.
The ledger also lists nominations for Dourif, cinematography, editing, and original score.
sources.limits: The 1976 ceremony follows the 1975 release; it supports awards and categories only.

retrieval_limits: The official Milos Forman page was attempted but did not return usable web-reader content; it is not used as evidence.
